title: A home for your infrastructure
description: How the local server, deployment pipeline, wiki, and observability portal fit together.
summary:
## The big picture
Your local server provides Qwen AI to NutsNews and hosts your observability portal. GitHub stores the instructions used to manage it. The wiki explains those instructions at three levels of detail.

## The three places to know
- **Observe** shows how your systems are doing.
- **GitHub Actions** checks and deploys changes.
- **This wiki** explains operation and recovery.

## What stays safe
The server is managed in place. Its data and Qwen models are preserved. NutsNews keeps using the existing AI address. You can read this wiki even when the local server is offline.
technical:
## Architecture
GitHub-hosted runners reach the Ubuntu server through Cloudflare Tunnel and machine-authenticated SSH. The portal runs locally under systemd and queries Grafana Cloud through a server-side API. The wiki is a static Astro site deployed independently to GitHub Pages.

## Repository ownership
| Repository | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| local-server-infra | Host provisioning and deployment coordinator |
| local-server-observability | Portal application, query catalog, and application release |
| local-server-wiki | Documentation, reading modes, and static publishing |

## Runtime boundaries
The SSH hostname is localserver.ramideltoro.com. The portal is observe.ramideltoro.com. The production AI route remains ai.nutsnews.com. No new interactive authentication is added to the AI endpoint.

## Changes
Build, validation, and documentation checks precede deployment. The release manifest binds code and documentation versions.
expert:
## Why separate code, documentation, and telemetry
Infrastructure changes have administrative reach; a portal frontend change should not implicitly have that scope. Separate repositories make ownership and release evidence explicit. The infrastructure coordinator serializes host mutations even when builds originate in different repositories.

## Failure domains
Local hosting makes the portal dependent on the host it describes. Cloud telemetry storage and independent wiki hosting preserve two recovery paths: evidence and instructions. A tunnel outage can prevent automated recovery; a LAN or console path remains necessary.

## Adoption instead of replacement
Rebuilding a functioning host would introduce avoidable risks to model files, credentials, and workers. Adoption records the current state and applies bounded changes. A clean-machine reconstruction is a distinct workflow, not an excuse to overwrite the running server.

## Architectural limits
The portal is an investigation surface, not a second production control plane. Existing NutsNews repositories retain ownership of their resources unless a reviewed migration explicitly transfers that ownership.

title: Find your way around
description: Choose a reading level and find the information you need.
summary:
## Start with the question
If you want to know whether things are working, open the observability portal. If you want to understand a component, search this wiki. If you need to change it, follow the GitHub workflow instructions.

## Choose your reading preference
**Summary** gives you the essentials. **Technical** describes configuration and operation. **Expert** explains the reasoning and tradeoffs. The top-right selector keeps you on the same topic. Your browser remembers your preference.

## Follow the evidence
A green website check means the endpoint responded. It does not prove every worker or database is healthy. Use the owner view for deeper investigation.
technical:
## Reading modes and navigation
Each topic has routes under /summary/, /technical/, and /expert/. The initial preference is Technical. Selecting a mode stores a browser-local preference; explicit deep links continue to open the requested version.

## Search
The sidebar search filters topic titles. Press / to focus it. On small screens, navigation becomes a horizontally scrollable topic strip while the mode selector stays near the top.

## Investigation workflow
1. Open the public overview and choose a time range.
2. Sign in to the owner view for private diagnostics.
3. Select the application and a dashboard.
4. Correlate its metrics with logs and deployment identity.
5. Open the corresponding recovery topic before making a change.

## Source of truth
Every repository README links here. Detailed procedures belong in this repository, avoiding competing copies across application repositories.
expert:
## Audience adaptation is a content contract
The three modes must explain the same system, but are not generated by simply hiding paragraphs. Summary prioritizes practical meaning. Technical specifies interfaces. Expert records alternatives, assumptions, and failure reasoning. CI verifies that every topic has three nonidentical, substantial versions.

## Preferences versus explicit intent
Browser storage affects the default landing experience only. An explicit /expert/ link is an intentional choice and must not be overridden by a previously saved Summary preference. This preserves reproducible sharing and avoids redirect loops.

## Meaning of health
Availability, correctness, timeliness, and capacity are different properties. The interface labels endpoint checks as reachability and keeps worker health and telemetry freshness separate. Missing samples must not become zero-valued measurements or green status.

title: The local server
description: The host, its services, and how it is managed without reinstalling it.
summary:
## What runs here
The server runs Qwen through Ollama, the NutsNews local AI API, telemetry collection, backups, and the observability portal. It has 16 logical CPUs and about 59 GiB of usable memory.

## How it is managed
GitHub applies the recorded configuration to the existing machine. Normal releases do not wipe disks, reinstall the operating system, or delete models. The AI services are left running when changes concern only documentation or the portal.

## What to watch
Look at CPU, available memory, storage, service state, and backup freshness together. A low CPU reading alone does not prove an application is healthy.
technical:
## Baseline
The adopted host runs Ubuntu 26.04 on an AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with 16 logical CPUs. The root filesystem has roughly 1.8 TiB capacity. Observability uses the stable instance label chingadera to join the existing metrics.

## Managed services
The baseline includes nutsnews-local-ai, ollama, cloudflared, alloy, backup timers, and health-check timers. The portal is a separate local-server-observability service with a loopback HTTP listener.

## Application protection
Existing AI unit definitions, model files, environment files, and routes are captured before management changes. Provisioning uses explicit handlers rather than restarting unrelated services on each run.

## Access
Administrative access is GitHub Actions over Cloudflare-proxied SSH. The LAN login remains the recovery path if the tunnel is unavailable. Credentials are not stored in this public repository.
expert:
## Resource isolation
Inference is the production workload. A metrics portal must not compete aggressively for memory or CPU. The portal service has bounded memory and CPU, query concurrency limits, and caching. Telemetry collection avoids expensive repeated process scans or inference probes in the normal page-refresh path.

## Reconciliation semantics
A configuration-management run should converge on a declared state without causing work on an already-correct host. Adoption and restoration are different operations: restoration may create missing files, while adoption must not overwrite unknown live state simply because a template exists.

## Recovery boundary
Configuration-as-code can reproduce services above a functioning OS. It cannot reach a host with a dead disk, broken network, or missing connector. Documentation must distinguish those prerequisites from a successful application rollout.

title: Qwen & production workers
description: The compatibility contract that keeps NutsNews connected to local AI.
summary:
## The promise
NutsNews continues to use the existing Qwen AI service. Its public address, authentication, model, and request format are preserved while the new infrastructure is added.

## What is checked
The pipeline checks the AI endpoint and makes a small real inference request. Success must come from **local Qwen**. A response from a fallback provider does not count.

## During other updates
Updating the portal or wiki does not restart Qwen or its API. If a change affects AI connectivity, the release is stopped or rolled back until the worker connection works again.

## Workload visibility
The Qwen page now shows aggregate requests, errors, in-flight work, model availability, and latency. Initial instrumentation needs a guarded API-wrapper restart after two idle checks; it does not restart Ollama or change the model. If demand stays busy, deployment is deferred. Later unchanged portal releases do not restart the wrapper.
technical:
## Existing interface
The route ai.nutsnews.com forwards through the existing tunnel to the loopback local AI API on port 8788. Ollama listens on port 11434 and provides qwen2.5:3b.

## Authentication and requests
Authenticated requests use the x-nutsnews-ai-key header. Existing endpoints include GET /health, GET /stats, POST /review, and POST /translate. Translation language support is defined by the deployed API; the compatibility probe uses French.

## Release gate
Verify health and model availability, send a synthetic translation request, and require provider=local, model=qwen2.5:3b, and a successful response. Record duration without recording prompt or response contents. Compare the AI service process identity before and after unrelated releases.

## Worker path
Check production-worker configuration and connectivity from its deployment environment. A direct developer-machine probe establishes endpoint health but is not a substitute for evidence from the worker path.

## Cloudflare Workers compatibility probe
A dedicated authenticated compatibility worker calls the unchanged production AI route from the Cloudflare Workers runtime. Deployment verifies local-provider and Qwen-model identity before and after changes. The probe has no schedules, database writes, or production worker configuration changes.

## Additive instrumentation
The API wrapper exports fixed-label counters, in-flight gauges, and latency histograms on loopback port 8791, scraped directly by Alloy. Background summary counts are separate. Queue depth inside Ollama is unavailable and labeled as a gap. The existing review/translate contract returns JSON and uses upstream stream=false; a stream flag does not change that behavior. Contract tests cover concurrent requests, authentication, timeout errors, and unchanged streaming behavior.

The installer checks the known live source hash, waits for two idle socket checks, saves the old source, sets a graceful stop timeout, and upgrades only the wrapper. A source mismatch or continuous traffic stops the rollout. Same-hash subsequent releases only verify the telemetry endpoint. Real local-provider and Cloudflare Worker inference gates run before and after rollout.
expert:
## Why a health check is insufficient
A healthy HTTP wrapper can coexist with a missing model, failed inference, or credentials that workers cannot use. The gate therefore verifies model identity and an authenticated inference response. Fallback success must be excluded because it can hide a broken local dependency while increasing cost.

## Routing isolation
Cloudflare Access protects deployment SSH only. Google sign-in protects owner diagnostics in the portal application. Protecting the whole zone or reusing an interactive policy on the AI route would break unattended workers. Tunnel configuration changes preserve every unrelated ingress rule and the existing AI mapping.

## Restart and rollout constraints
The model may need several gigabytes of memory and time to load. Unrelated releases must not unload it. A real AI update should use a tested parallel instance where possible and drain active requests. If parallel operation cannot fit within host capacity, zero downtime must not be claimed.

## Privacy
Synthetic probe content is harmless, but production article bodies, prompts, outputs, and credential values are never telemetry labels or public diagnostic artifacts.

## Runtime evidence
The dedicated probe establishes that Cloudflare Workers can authenticate and complete real Qwen inference through the existing tunnel. It complements production worker configuration and health evidence; it does not claim to run a full production article-processing job or validate unrelated worker stages.

## Instrumentation boundaries
Request aggregates use only fixed operation/workload labels. No prompts, responses, credentials, or user identifiers are collected. In-flight work is not a queue-depth estimate. Idle-only AI summaries keep one request at a time and a five-minute total budget; busy or unavailable inference produces a template. The initial wrapper upgrade uses an idle window, so a brief wrapper restart is possible and zero downtime is not claimed. Ollama, production routing, authentication, model configuration, and worker contracts are preserved. The upgraded wrapper drains requests on future graceful shutdowns.

title: GitHub deployment pipeline
description: From a reviewed change to a verified release on the server.
summary:
## How a release works
A change is checked in GitHub, matched to its documentation, built, and deployed. The pipeline then checks that the portal responds and Qwen still works. You do not need to run a command on your Mac for normal releases.

## One change at a time
Server deployments are serialized so two repositories cannot update the same host at once. A failed check prevents a release from being marked successful.

## Recovery
The previous application release is retained. Use the rollback workflow if a new portal release fails its checks.
technical:
## Workflow responsibilities
The observability repository builds and tests the application. The wiki repository validates and publishes all reading modes. The infrastructure repository coordinates the host deployment and verifies documentation fingerprints.

## Release manifest
A release records infrastructure, portal, and wiki revisions. Deployment uses the validated revisions rather than resolving a moving branch halfway through the run. The coordinator serializes host changes and exposes manual status and rollback operations.

## Gates
Required checks include application tests, production build, documentation-source matching, SSH host identity, AI health and inference, portal health, and post-deployment AI compatibility.

## Credentials
GitHub secret values are materialized only inside the trusted deployment job. Untrusted pull-request code is never run with production credentials.
expert:
## Cross-repository consistency
Git repositories do not provide a distributed transaction. A release manifest supplies the missing association: it identifies exactly which code and documentation were validated together. Publishing versioned documentation before runtime activation avoids shipping an undocumented behavior, while the current-version pointer changes only after verification.

## Concurrency and retries
GitHub concurrency is repository-scoped, so every host mutation passes through one coordinator. Retries must be idempotent and may safely resume after a transient tunnel disconnect. Changes to the connector itself run last because a broken connector can strand the deployment job.

## Rollback limits
Switching a symlink can roll back application code, but does not undo arbitrary data migrations. This release introduces no production application schema migration. Baseline service files and sensitive settings require explicit backups and carefully scoped restoration.

title: Tunnels & access
description: Independent routes for production AI, deployment SSH, and the portal.
summary:
## A secure path into the server
Cloudflare Tunnel makes outbound connections from your server. GitHub uses a protected SSH route to deploy, and browsers use the portal route to view health.

## Separate doors
The production AI address is unchanged. The owner view requires sign-in, while public health pages do not. These routes have separate access rules so a new login requirement cannot accidentally block NutsNews workers.

## If the tunnel goes down
The local portal and remote deployments may become unreachable. Grafana Cloud and this independently hosted wiki remain available for investigation.
technical:
## Hostnames
| Hostname | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| ai.nutsnews.com | Existing production AI API |
| localserver.ramideltoro.com | Machine-authenticated deployment SSH |
| observe.ramideltoro.com | Public portal and authenticated owner routes |
| localserver.wiki.ramideltoro.com | Independent GitHub Pages wiki |

## SSH
The GitHub runner uses cloudflared as an SSH ProxyCommand. A dedicated Access service token authenticates the tunnel connection, and an SSH key authenticates to the host. Host-key verification remains enabled.

## Owner routes
The Node backend protects /owner and /api/owner with a secure Google-authenticated owner session. Cloudflare Access must not intercept these portal paths. Public responses use a fixed allowlist and contain no raw operational logs.
expert:
## Two independent authentication layers
An Access token authorizes reaching the SSH application; an SSH key authorizes a host login. Neither should replace the other. Pinning the SSH host key prevents DNS or route changes from silently substituting another machine.

## Origin validation
An HTTP header alone is not proof of identity. The backend validates Google ID-token signatures, issuer, audience, expiration, nonce, verified email and the owner allowlist before issuing an application session. It never trusts identity headers. A loopback listener prevents the application from exposing an unprotected LAN port.

## DNS and certificate boundaries
The wiki uses its own DNS-only GitHub Pages record and HTTPS certificate. It is a nested subdomain, so relying on a Cloudflare certificate that covers only one subdomain level would be incorrect. Portal and SSH records use the existing tunnel, preserving its production AI ingress rule.

title: Public observability workspace
description: Public native dashboards, server navigation and owner changes.
summary:
## Read without signing in
The dark amber portal brings servers and applications together. Start with the fleet overview, then open a server or its applications from the sidebar. The mobile menu contains the same navigation. Dashboards, issue reports and alert explanations are public.

## Change with Google
Use Google sign-in to open full diagnostics and editable Grafana copies. Public visitors cannot save dashboards, change configuration or start inspections. The existing NutsNews AI endpoint remains available to production workers.

## Understand coverage
Some panels need private logs or Cloud-only plugins. Those panels explain the limitation and link to an owner or Cloud view. Missing values mean unavailable telemetry, not zero usage. All discovered dashboards remain listed.

## Health comes first
The overview starts with passing endpoint checks, failing core checks, servers within resource limits, and servers whose telemetry cannot be verified. Green means passing, red means a failing check, and grey means unknown. Select an endpoint or server to investigate. The interface uses native macOS typography where available, a dark amber palette, compact utilization meters, and a mobile navigation drawer.
technical:
## Runtime architecture
The Node portal listens on loopback 4310 and exposes collector metrics on 4311. Two Grafana 13.2.1 instances listen on loopback 4320 and 4321. Public Grafana has no Grafana Cloud credentials; its Prometheus datasource calls a loopback gateway on 4312. The owner instance receives a Cloud read token and a trusted identity only after the portal verifies the Google session.

## Public query contract
Queries are registered in Git from the approved metric catalog. Grafana submits opaque query identifiers. The gateway never forwards client PromQL. It validates time bounds, maximum seven days, at most 400 steps, 24 series, six concurrent upstream requests and a two-megabyte response budget. Series labels are replaced with anonymous names. Public query POSTs work; dashboard saves and other mutation routes are denied.

## Dashboard synchronization
The synchronization job discovers Cloud dashboards and preserves original definitions in the owner instance. Public definitions preserve supported panel types and positions while removing private links, annotations, variables, text and raw expressions. Queries absent from the registry and unsupported plugins become explained restrictions. Source providers disallow UI updates; editable copies use separate UIDs. The catalog includes legacy portal dashboards and published workspace dashboards.

## Overview health semantics
The health header separates current endpoint probes and CPU/memory/root-disk pressure from persistent daily findings. A server is within limits only when all three resource metrics are live, finite, and no older than five minutes. CPU or memory at 90%, or disk at 85%, indicates resource pressure. The worst latest series value is used. Missing or stale series are unverified, never zero. A known threshold breach remains failing even when another resource is unknown. Endpoint probes map healthy to passing, degraded/unavailable to failing, and stale overview responses to unverified. These are display checks, not additional alert evaluators. Existing Cloud rule timing and pending periods are unchanged. Critical daily findings appear first below the health section.
expert:
## Why two Grafana instances
A Viewer role alone does not constrain what a datasource credential can read. A separate public process, filesystem identity and restricted gateway make the public credential boundary explicit. The public process has no unrestricted Cloud token and cannot read the owner configuration. Loopback binding also prevents bypassing portal routing from the network.

## Public projection tradeoffs
A native panel may depend on labels, transformations, variables, proprietary plugins or sensitive text. Publishing it verbatim would defeat sanitization. The public projection preserves supported metric visualization and layout while replacing private series labels and explaining unsupported content. Fixed query scope avoids treating arbitrary regular expressions as trusted dashboard parameters.

## Failure and ownership
Both Grafana processes have independent resource limits. Alert evaluation remains in Cloud to avoid duplicate notifications and independent state machines. Qwen and Ollama services are not restarted by portal deployment. The existing before-and-after inference checks remain release gates. A local portal outage does not remove Cloud telemetry or the independently hosted wiki.

## Visual hierarchy and uncertainty
The first screen answers whether current probes are passing and whether host resources need attention. Resource health cannot prove every application is healthy, and a passing endpoint cannot resolve a historical issue; the UI keeps live core checks and daily findings distinct. Neutral unverified states avoid claiming an offline telemetry source is either a confirmed outage or a healthy host. Text accompanies status colors, utilization bars supplement numeric values, and the native Apple system font falls back to platform sans-serif without downloading proprietary fonts. Responsive lists, keyboard focus states, and reduced-motion support preserve the same investigation paths on mobile.

title: NutsNews service map
description: Follow the application from its public endpoints to workers and data services.
summary:
## Follow the application
NutsNews depends on its website, backend, workers, databases, queues, and AI providers. The portal brings these signals together so you can move from a symptom to the responsible service.

## Start with impact
Check public availability first, then request latency, errors, ingestion freshness, and worker progress. If a worker is delayed, inspect its queue and dependencies rather than assuming the whole website is down.

## Local AI
The local Qwen server is one dependency in this map. Its connectivity and inference checks remain mandatory during local-server releases.

## Opening private diagnostics
Select NutsNews, then Sign in with Google for owner diagnostics. If your session expires, sign in again; a login failure is not evidence that NutsNews is down.

## Dedicated VPS views
Backend VPS and NutsNews VPS now have separate navigation entries. Each shows its own CPU, memory, root disk and system load. Sign in with Google to inspect its detailed dashboards and use the host selector in Logs.
technical:
## Existing coverage
The catalog includes application service health, both VPS hosts, backend API, PostgreSQL operations and failover, RabbitMQ queues and resources, worker pipeline SLOs, deployment ownership, backups, synthetic checks, logs, and usage quotas.

## Production versus shadow
Worker deployment metrics distinguish active production ownership from shadow deployments. A stopped shadow service is not automatically a production outage. Use expected-active and deployment-identity signals when interpreting health.

## Correlation
Start with the affected time range and service. Inspect request rates and error changes, then logs, queue depth, and deployment revision. Follow existing provider diagnostics for signals outside Grafana.

## Instrumentation
Add bounded metrics or structured diagnostic fields only where a concrete gap prevents investigation. Preserve current behavior and the established NutsNews resource ownership.

## Owner sign-in
Private dashboards use the portal Google session and preserve the NutsNews tab through authentication. Google OAuth changes apply to this observability portal, not the production workers or Qwen API.

## Host isolation
Backend VPS selects instance backend.nutsnews.com; NutsNews VPS selects instance vps.nutsnews.com. The catalog groups backend database, Docker, backups and services under Backend VPS and the existing VPS resource dashboards under NutsNews VPS. The NutsNews application library still includes both groups. Log queries use fixed host selectors rather than arbitrary client-supplied expressions.
expert:
## Dependency health versus user impact
A queue, a worker, and a website expose different failure surfaces. Queue depth can rise during normal throughput bursts; errors can increase while fallback preserves availability. Combining expected ownership, queue age, terminal outcomes, and public synthetic checks prevents misleading incident conclusions.

## Existing telemetry policy
NutsNews already defines a signal budget and permitted label taxonomy. Importing dashboards does not authorize unlimited new telemetry. Existing policy defers some trace and profile export. The portal exposes trace availability honestly and should not infer completeness merely from the presence of a Tempo datasource.

## Source ownership
The central portal reads existing metrics rather than taking over every NutsNews provisioning pipeline. This avoids two repositories fighting over the same Grafana or server resource. New ownership is explicit; migrations require a single writer and a documented handoff.

## Separate authentication from telemetry
A 401 means the browser needs a new owner session. Treat it independently from a source query failure or an empty series. Google ID verification and authorization happen on the portal server; Grafana tokens never enter the browser.

## Application versus host views
The application spans multiple machines. Separate host views prevent an average from obscuring a saturated machine, while the combined NutsNews library preserves cross-service investigation. These additions reuse existing Grafana collection and do not install another agent or restart production workers.

title: Logs, traces & privacy
description: Find useful diagnostic evidence without exposing private records.
summary:
## Different kinds of evidence
Metrics show trends. Logs explain events. Traces connect steps in a request when that instrumentation exists. The owner view brings these forms of evidence together.

## Private details stay private
Raw logs, internal host details, and diagnostic records require sign-in. Public pages show only selected summaries. Credentials and sensitive values are removed from diagnostic text where possible.

## Missing traces
If a service does not export traces, the portal says so. An empty trace view is not proof that the service is healthy.
technical:
## Logs
Owner log queries are bounded by application, time range, and a literal search string. The backend escapes the search value rather than accepting arbitrary LogQL. Results are capped and ordered newest first.

## Traces
The owner endpoint discovers the existing Tempo datasource and requests a bounded search. A datasource can exist without ingesting traces. Preserve the worker telemetry policy when deciding whether to enable additional exports.

## Data handling
Public endpoints never return raw logs or trace payloads. Server-side credentials do not enter browser bundles. Redaction removes common credential patterns and email addresses before diagnostic lines are returned.

## Correlation
Use timestamps and available trace/run identifiers to move between service metrics and individual diagnostic records.
expert:
## Redaction is defense in depth
Pattern matching cannot reliably sanitize arbitrary secrets or production content. Collection must avoid emitting sensitive data in the first place. Authentication and explicit public schemas remain the primary boundaries; redaction reduces incidental exposure inside the owner view.

## Cardinality and payload rules
Run IDs and trace IDs belong in bounded diagnostic records, not unconstrained metric labels. Production article text, prompts, model outputs, and tokens must not be copied into new telemetry. This matters both for privacy and for avoiding runaway series counts.

## Trace rollout
If trace export is added, propagate context through the actual request and queue boundaries and verify a complete sample. Respect the existing sampling ceiling, retention, and quota controls. Do not present a synthetic trace or disconnected spans as proof of production end-to-end coverage.

title: Alerts & telemetry freshness
description: Separate real failures from missing measurements and expected inactivity.
summary:
## What needs attention
Alerts highlight sustained failures, resource pressure, and overdue backups. A brief spike should not become a flood of notifications. Existing alert contacts and rules are reused.

## Freshness matters
A chart can look calm because nothing new is arriving. The portal marks missing or old data explicitly. Check collection health before trusting a quiet graph.

## When the portal is down
Cloud-based checks continue to monitor the local endpoint. Use Grafana directly and open the recovery instructions in this wiki.

## Complete rule catalog
The public Alert rules page lists configured rules, including healthy and paused rules. It reads actual evaluation intervals from Cloud rule-group metadata; observed groups evaluate every 60 or 300 seconds. Pending duration and lookback are separate fields. Silenced rules remain enabled unless paused. Private expressions require owner diagnostics. Missing evaluation metadata is shown as unknown rather than inferred from query resolution.
technical:
## Default additions
Local-server checks cover missing telemetry, required service failure, CPU or memory above 90% for ten minutes, disk usage above 85% for fifteen minutes, and overdue backups using their actual schedule.

## Existing rules
Retain current NutsNews thresholds and notification routing. The portal queries the existing Grafana alert source and distinguishes query failure from an empty active-alert list.

## Freshness
Metric results with no samples are unavailable. Samples older than three minutes are stale in the portal. The HTTP response timestamp describes retrieval time, not necessarily measurement time.

## Verification
Test new alert expressions with representative synthetic inputs. Verify recovery as well as firing, and avoid intentionally disrupting production services for routine validation.

## Complete rule catalog
The public Alert rules page lists configured rules, including healthy and paused rules. It reads actual evaluation intervals from Cloud rule-group metadata; observed groups evaluate every 60 or 300 seconds. Pending duration and lookback are separate fields. Silenced rules remain enabled unless paused. Private expressions require owner diagnostics. Missing evaluation metadata is shown as unknown rather than inferred from query resolution.
expert:
## Avoiding false reassurance
An empty alert list can mean all rules are normal, a source is unreachable, rules are absent, or data is missing. The application must expose source failures and never infer universal health from that one list. Likewise, transport uptime and service correctness are independent signals.

## Threshold duration
Sustained windows filter scheduler noise and short bursts. They should not delay fast availability alerts: a required service outage needs a shorter window than high CPU. Backup deadlines depend on schedule rather than a universal fixed duration.

## Independent monitoring
The portal cannot reliably report its own total outage. Its external synthetic check and cloud alert evaluation form the independent failure detector. Notification routing remains in the existing provider rather than adding another competing alert engine.

## Complete rule catalog
The public Alert rules page lists configured rules, including healthy and paused rules. It reads actual evaluation intervals from Cloud rule-group metadata; observed groups evaluate every 60 or 300 seconds. Pending duration and lookback are separate fields. Silenced rules remain enabled unless paused. Private expressions require owner diagnostics. Missing evaluation metadata is shown as unknown rather than inferred from query resolution.

title: Backups & recovery
description: Protect existing data and know which recovery path to use.
summary:
## Keep the existing backups
The infrastructure rollout preserves backup files, destinations, and schedules. The portal shows whether backups are recent and whether restore verification has evidence.

## Choose the right recovery
For a broken portal release, roll back the application. For a configuration problem, restore the relevant saved configuration. For a failed disk or operating system, use the machine recovery process before GitHub can reconnect.

## Keep this page available
The wiki is hosted independently so you can still read recovery instructions when the local server is offline.

## Read the outcome and the timestamp
The portal shows image and database backups separately. A running timer does not mean its last backup succeeded. Check the last outcome, the age of the backup, and the age of the status report.

## Application restore drills
Backups and completed recovery tests have separate results. The local server restores saved data and application files in a disposable environment with no production network access. Successful evidence expires after eight days or when the deployed application changes. A failed test stays failed.

## Worker recovery
Six NutsNews workers are tested one at a time from encrypted cloud backups. The test restores their saved work and broker, checks readiness, and confirms that a completed message is not processed again. Production workers are not activated or restarted. This does not measure production throughput or prove a full pipeline cutover. Failed, missing, expired or changed-revision evidence remains unverified.

## ShowAlgo recovery
ShowAlgo recovery uses the actual Firebase deployment and its hosting rules. Every deployed file must match Firebase’s checksum before an encrypted backup can pass. The downloaded backup is served privately to verify its files, page routes and cache headers. The live website is not redeployed.

## Raspberry backup readiness
A daily encrypted backup streams the Pi root filesystem and boot files to the local server, then to the existing cloud destination. This avoids using the nearly full SD card for temporary backup files. A verified downloaded archive proves backup readiness only; boot and full application restoration remain unverified. The disconnected receiver stays inactive.
technical:
## Baseline jobs
Adopt existing database and home-server image backup timers, health checks, and backup-status metric generation. Inspect the installed schedules and destinations before managing them.

## Application rollback
The deployment stores versioned portal releases and the previous active target. Rollback reactivates a retained verified release and checks both the portal and Qwen connection. It must not overwrite application data.

## Configuration recovery
Sensitive configuration snapshots are stored outside public Git. Restore only the affected files, validate them, and reload the relevant service. Preserve unrelated tunnel routes and the production AI environment.

## Full-host recovery
Restore or install Ubuntu, establish network and SSH access, enroll the tunnel connector, then run the provisioning workflow. Model downloads and data restoration may require separate elapsed time.

## Local backup panels
A dedicated dashboard uses existing home_server_backup and nutsnews_db_backup metrics for outcomes, attempt age, archive size, duration, cloud copies, and status freshness. Local alert rules surface failed backup outcomes and stale status collection without changing any backup jobs.

## Recovery controller
The root-owned observe-recovery.timer polls deployments every fifteen minutes. The service shares /run/observe-recovery.lock, CPUQuota=200%, MemoryMax=8G, MemorySwapMax=0 and an isolated loopback network. Successful unchanged applications run weekly; failed attempts back off six hours. An application deployment invalidates its prior evidence. Only the controller writes /var/lib/observe-recovery/public/evidence.json; Observe reads sanitized status, scope and timestamps.

## Backup and restore path
Capture the deployed revision and its real saved data; encrypt with AES-256-GCM, upload to the existing homebackup encrypted remote, download and validate the encrypted hash and authentication tag, and restore into a disposable filesystem. Static sites rebuild archived deployed source and deployment configuration. KubeQuest reads restored SQLite progress through its private application route. Qwen instances execute isolated CPU inference using restored model blobs. Observe boots restored operations history, owner Grafana database, saved dashboard files and provisioning configuration. Restored provisioning paths point only inside the disposable filesystem; dashboard counts and individual dashboard reads must pass through the running Grafana API. Backend and Fantasy use restored PostgreSQL data and real application readiness and read routes. Readiness and full application behavior receive separate evidence.

## Cloud database backup
The adopted Supabase backup now archives the complete public schema and data, authentication schema definitions without rows, roles without passwords, and required extension declarations. The existing encrypted destination, schedule and retention remain unchanged. Use existing credentials and the production session pooler; never reset a password to repair a backup. The repeatable verify-cloud-database.mjs drill restores role names without production privileges or memberships, then the authentication schema, and injects extension prerequisites immediately after the public schema is recreated. Run it under the shared recovery lock with CPUQuota=200%, MemoryMax=8G and MemorySwapMax=0. Validate checksums, relational integrity and saved data.

## Credentials and operator access
Recovery credentials and the encryption key live under root-only /etc/observe-recovery. Key versions are preserved under their hash in the existing encrypted cloud destination. Restore the matching key privately; never place a key, database dump or detailed diagnostic evidence in a public repository. The backend exporter uses a pinned SSH host key and a forced-command identity with fixed read-only exports. It cannot select arbitrary commands, paths or restore targets.

## Verified database repair
On 2026-09-20, the existing production session-pooler credential repaired the authentication failure. The downloaded cloud backup nutsnews-db-2026-09-20_00-41-26 passed checksum validation and restored its complete public schema and 2,449 articles into disposable PostgreSQL. Backend snapshot 9b3b0868 passed its existing integrity verifier; an ExecStartPost verifier removes the former backup-to-verification timing gap. No passwords, backup destinations or retention policies changed.

## Dependency preparation boundary
The preparation phase downloads locked npm dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled. No application or package install hooks run with network access. Builds and restored application behavior run only in the disposable loopback-only network namespace.

## Personal website artifact recovery
The ramideltoro.com Netlify manual deployment is captured by immutable published deployment ID, not an assumed Git commit. Archive every file with its provider checksum plus hosting settings; reject deployments with server or edge functions. Download the encrypted cloud backup, verify all restored file hashes and serve every archived file inside the private recovery namespace. No production deployment is changed. NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN is stored only in the existing root-only recovery credential file.

## Observe log continuity
Each completed operations collection emits a bounded structured event containing only its event name and system count. This proves actual application work independently of dashboard visits; the existing scoped Loki selector and freshness requirement remain unchanged.

## Shared cloud backup safety
Image retention and image freshness inventory accept only the current hostname followed by the exact YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS directory format. Database and Observe recovery folders are never image-retention candidates. The existing policy of retaining the newest verified image backup remains unchanged. Both scripts are versioned and installed through the validated infrastructure release.

## Isolated worker recovery
The fixed backend exporter captures deployed worker files/configuration, populated PostgreSQL data and roles without passwords, sanitized broker topology and the broker runtime. All queues, including canary/retry/dead-letter queues, must be empty before and after capture. Restore the downloaded encrypted archive in the existing shared-lock namespace with 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and no swap. Bind restored Alpine musl/Erlang/RabbitMQ libraries read-only inside that namespace; no nested privileged container or production network is required. Preserve database roles and ACLs. Require real worker readiness, then publish a schema-valid synthetic carrier with an actual completed inbox identity. Require duplicate recognition, zero queued replay messages, unchanged inbox count and byte-equivalent completed record. Persistence/publication use the restored backend API; approval restores Qwen and executes isolated inference. This proves durable-state recovery and duplicate replay, not new-work throughput or cutover readiness. Weekly/current-revision/eight-day evidence rules are unchanged.

## Live image capture boundaries
Exclude virtual filesystems, the actively written system journal and temporary recovery staging from the root image. Keep ordinary application data, configuration and existing image retention/destination intact. Compression uses two threads at level six to reduce competition with production. An archive read error still fails the job; no general changed-file error suppression is used. Prior cloud images are removed only after a verified replacement upload.

## Latest-attempt truth
The backup status collector reads the durable latest-attempt state. A retained older cloud image proves availability of that image but must never turn a newer failed attempt into success.

Persistence also requires the original backed-up upstream outbox envelope and payload, with its aggregate/payload fingerprint matching the restored completed inbox row before replay. A synthetic carrier must not bypass that conflict check. Deployment identities are re-probed between weekly drills so earlier results stay current during a long serialized run.

## ShowAlgo Firebase artifact recovery
The observe-recovery-showalgo service account has only roles/firebasehosting.viewer on the showalgo project. The approved JSON credential is stored as SHOWALGO_FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64 in the central credentials file and root-only /etc/observe-recovery/credentials.env; never commit it or include it in an archive. OAuth tokens are short-lived and retained only in memory. Read the current finalized live version, its complete paginated file inventory and immutable ServingConfig. Download from the fixed showalgo.web.app origin without credentials, verifying each compressed SHA-256 against the provider inventory. CDN-decompressed binary files are recompressed at Firebase’s level-nine gzip format and must match that same hash. Capture rejects missing files, checksum failures, duplicate paths, unsupported serving features and a concurrent deployment. After encrypted cloud roundtrip, the isolated verifier checks every file, directory index routes, missing-file behavior and the supported cache headers. This proves recovery of the deployed static artifact and hosting configuration; it does not assert the old Git checkout corresponds to that deployment or prove a source rebuild. Unrecognized serving configuration remains failed until explicitly supported and tested. Weekly/revision/expiry and resource limits are unchanged.

## Raspberry off-host snapshots
The existing serialized recovery runner captures the root filesystem plus the separate boot files through a restricted SSH key and a fixed read-only exporter. Volatile files, package caches and swap contents are excluded; application data, installed packages and service configuration are retained. The runner encrypts, uploads, downloads and checks the archive and required members before recording readiness. Evidence renews daily, expires after 27 hours, and is invalidated by configuration/revision mismatch. Full restore evidence is not created. The local runner retains its 2 CPU / 8 GiB limits; Pi export uses low-priority streaming with no local snapshot file. Existing retention and application state remain unchanged.
expert:
## Backup existence is not restore evidence
A recent file can be incomplete or unreadable. Observability separates successful job completion, archive freshness, size, and restore-verification results. An untested backup should not be labeled recoverable solely because its timestamp is recent.

## Destructive boundaries
Adoption never formats a disk or replaces existing data. Restoration is explicit and scoped. Copying an entire baseline over a running machine risks reverting unrelated updates and credentials, so missing-file recovery and targeted rollback are distinct mechanisms.

## Failure ordering
If the tunnel fails, GitHub cannot perform normal SSH repair. If the host fails, the portal cannot serve diagnostics. Cloud history and the independently hosted wiki remain useful, but neither substitutes for a LAN or console recovery path.

## Stale evidence
A collector may continue exporting an old success or failure. Compare the collection timestamp with the job timestamp and cloud-object evidence. Keep failed outcomes distinct from absent metrics, and never infer restore success from a nonzero archive size.

## Evidence and failure semantics
A backup upload never establishes full restoration. A passing restore requires archive integrity, isolated-network verification, real restored data and representative application behavior. Invalid or missing evidence, expired timestamps, or a changed deployment yield unverified status; a failed attempted recovery is a failure. A current deployment observation must be younger than twenty minutes. Scoring weights, category thresholds, system membership and availability-history requirements are unchanged. Missing application log streams stay unverified, even if an error query is empty.

## Rollback and acceptance
Stop the recovery timer to pause new drills; existing encrypted backups and production applications remain intact. Revert the scoped collector/recovery release through the validated deployment workflow. A successful rollout requires actual fleet health of at least 70 percent twice, fifteen minutes apart, healthy endpoints and no unexpected production process changes. Qwen request logging uses the existing idle-gated update and rollback procedure; only the wrapper is restarted after a verified idle interval, while Ollama remains running.

The 76-percent improvement acceptance uses two fresh actual fleet readings at least fifteen minutes apart, with no dip below the target during observation. Independent production ingestion freshness can reduce the fleet score even when every new recovery drill passes. Never relax that freshness contract to meet the target.

### Raspberry backup boundary
The dedicated key can invoke only revision or archive on /usr/local/sbin/observe-raspberry-export. Its known host key is pinned. A narrow sudoers entry permits these fixed operations; arbitrary commands, tunnels and PTYs are not permitted. Required members include boot config/cmdline, fstab, os-release, readsb runtime/service and dpkg status. Corrupt, missing or changed snapshots cannot pass readiness. No Raspberry restore method is registered, so archive verification never awards isolated-restore credit. The required Raspberry repositories were not resolvable during implementation; this operations runbook records the cross-host mechanism without substituting it for those repositories.

title: Documentation that follows code
description: How release checks keep all three reading versions aligned with implementation.
summary:
## Documentation is part of a release
A behavior change needs matching documentation before it can deploy. Each affected topic includes Summary, Technical, and Expert versions.

## What the checks do
GitHub compares the recorded code fingerprint with the candidate release. Missing or outdated documentation stops the deployment instead of letting the wiki quietly fall behind.

## Versions matter
The release records which code and documentation belong together. Failed deployments are not marked current, and rollback points readers back to the matching behavior.
technical:
## Source matching
Each code repository exposes a deterministic fingerprint of its implementation and workflow files. The wiki stores those fingerprints in sources.lock.json. The deployment gate computes the candidate fingerprint and compares it with the validated wiki revision.

## Authoring workflow
Update the affected topic in all three modes, update factual inventories, and refresh the source lock. Validate all topics and build the static site. Merge the documentation revision before the matching runtime release proceeds.

## Release evidence
The deployment manifest records the code and documentation SHAs. Daily checks detect missing synchronization events. A mismatch is reported as a failed gate rather than silently updating prose from code.

## README role
Repository READMEs describe purpose and entry points. Detailed operational instructions remain here.
expert:
## What a fingerprint proves
A hash proves which bytes were associated with documentation; it does not prove the prose is correct. Review must still verify behavior and reasoning. Automated validation checks coverage, route integrity, and distinct reading versions, while the source lock prevents unnoticed code drift.

## Avoiding circular versions
Documentation hashes should not include generated deployment evidence that changes on every run. The lock binds implementation and workflow files; the release manifest adds the final commit identities afterward. This avoids a never-ending cycle of code SHA and wiki SHA updates.

## Publication ordering
Cross-repository release steps are not atomic. Validate and publish the documented version first, activate runtime second, and record successful deployment last. Failures retain the prior runtime and make the mismatch explicit instead of pretending synchronization succeeded.

title: Add another application
description: Extend the portal without changing the production AI contract.
summary:
## Start with the application
Decide which user-facing outcome matters, then identify its services and existing monitoring. Add an application entry and connect the relevant metrics and diagnostics.

## Keep the public view simple
Public pages should show selected health information. Detailed logs and internal dependencies belong in the owner view.

## Finish the whole change
Add the application documentation in all three reading modes, verify the new charts, and deploy through GitHub. Existing applications and Qwen must keep working.
technical:
## Integration steps
1. Identify the existing telemetry source and resource owner.
2. Add a bounded application identifier and curated query catalog entries.
3. Add source credentials server-side only if an existing datasource is insufficient.
4. Choose explicit public aggregate fields; keep detailed labels private.
5. Add applicable dashboards, alerts, and runbooks.
6. Update all reading modes and the documentation fingerprint.

## Validation
Compare returned values with the source query, exercise stale and unavailable states, and verify access separation. Ensure new collection does not exceed the current signal budget.

## Ownership
Adding an application to the central interface does not move its deployment pipeline into the local-server repository.
expert:
## A catalog rather than arbitrary query access
An extensible system can still have bounded interfaces. Curated query identifiers make caching, testing, and public/private review tractable. Exposing a generic datasource proxy would turn the portal into a much broader data-access surface.

## Integration versus migration
Centralizing investigation is usually less disruptive than centralizing every service's infrastructure ownership. Preserve one writer for each resource. If ownership must move, import existing state and disable the old writer before enabling the new one.

## Acceptance criteria
The integration is complete only when the application can be diagnosed from symptoms to dependencies with real evidence. Empty charts and links alone are not a substitute for working telemetry. Document any unavailable signal explicitly and retain the established production compatibility checks.

title: Rami Del Toro and ShowAlgo
description: Continuous HTTPS telemetry for the personal website and ShowAlgo.
summary:
## Your websites in one place
The portal now includes www.ramideltoro.com and www.showalgo.com. Each has its own sidebar view, health card, and history charts. The local server checks both once a minute even when the portal is closed.

## What the signals mean
Availability shows successful checks during the last hour. Response time shows how quickly the site starts responding. HTTP status identifies errors, and certificate remaining shows when HTTPS renewal is due. New history starts when monitoring is deployed.

## Coverage
These are website reachability checks, not visitor analytics or a full browser speed test. Hosting resource usage and application logs are not connected. A local-server outage also interrupts these checks.
technical:
## Collection
The portal Node process runs two fixed HTTPS GET probes every 60 seconds with an 8-second deadline and standard TLS certificate verification. Only response headers are measured; response bodies and cookies are discarded. Redirects are not followed and count as unsuccessful, since the monitored URLs are expected to return a successful page directly.

## Storage and dashboard
The loopback metrics endpoint exports website_probe_success, website_probe_duration_seconds, website_probe_status_code, website_probe_certificate_expiry_timestamp_seconds and website_probe_last_check_timestamp_seconds. The website label is limited to ramideltoro or showalgo. Existing Alloy scrapes port 4311 once a minute and writes into Grafana Cloud. Public views provide four curated metrics; owner dashboards add time since the last probe.

## Interpretation
Rolling-hour availability uses avg_over_time over stored success samples, not an externally measured SLA. HTTP status zero indicates no HTTP response. Missing certificate data is omitted. Historical data accumulates after deployment. A check older than three minutes is unavailable.

## Releases
The observability repository owns the probe definitions and dashboard catalog. Its workflow dispatches the infrastructure pipeline, which checks documentation fingerprints and production Qwen compatibility before and after activation.

## Verified static recovery
The personal site uses its immutable Netlify deployment; ShowAlgo uses its finalized Firebase Hosting version and complete checksum inventory. Both recover the actual deployed artifact from an encrypted cloud copy in the isolated local recovery environment. Hosting application logs remain unconfigured and availability history continues accumulating normally. See Backups & recovery for identity permissions, supported serving configuration and evidence expiry.
expert:
## Why active checks
HTTPS probes give consistent availability evidence across hosting providers without installing visitor trackers or collecting user data. The fixed target list avoids exposing an arbitrary URL fetcher. Requests have bounded duration, bounded concurrency and no retained page content. TLS verification stays enabled, so certificate failures become availability failures rather than being hidden.

## Measurement boundaries
Response time ends at arrival of HTTP headers, excluding full asset loading and rendering. Success means a 2xx response, not proof that every page feature works. Redirects intentionally fail the expected URL contract. Certificate lifetime describes the certificate served to this probe, which may differ across CDN edges.

## Failure domains and missing samples
Both probes run from the local server and therefore share its internet and power dependencies. Grafana retains history independently, but a host outage produces a telemetry gap rather than evidence that both websites are down. Rolling availability covers observed scrape samples only; consult collection freshness before interpreting it. Multiple external locations would be needed for a stronger public availability objective.

## Extensions
Connect hosting logs, deploy events, real-user performance or application metrics separately when access and a concrete investigation need exist. Do not label those signals as present until verified. Preserve the fixed label budget and never add visitor identifiers, URLs with query strings, or response content to metric labels.

title: Fantasy Football Edge telemetry
description: Website and database connectivity monitoring for Fantasy Football Edge.
summary:
## What is monitored
Fantasy Football Edge has a dedicated view in Observe. The local server checks its public website and backend health once a minute. The backend health check also verifies that the application can reach PostgreSQL.

## Reading the view
The page shows availability, response time, HTTP status, certificate lifetime and backend health. Owner diagnostics add collection freshness and backend response time. History starts when these checks were deployed.

## Scope
This does not measure fantasy forecast accuracy, importer freshness or individual league operations. A healthy database connection does not prove the importer has new Yahoo data.
technical:
## Endpoints
The monitor requests https://fantasy.ramideltoro.com and https://fantasy.ramideltoro.com/healthz every 60 seconds. The application health handler runs SELECT 1 before returning status ok, so a successful health response includes a database connectivity check.

## Metrics
The website label fantasy identifies frontend HTTPS telemetry; fantasy-health identifies the backend check. Both export success, response-header duration, status code, certificate expiry and last check time through the portal loopback metrics endpoint. Alloy stores samples in Grafana Cloud. Public views expose curated aggregates, while the owner catalog includes all seven telemetry panels.

## Protection
TLS verification is enabled, checks stop after eight seconds, redirects fail the expected direct URL contract, and response bodies are discarded. No Google sessions, Yahoo credentials or league records are collected.

## Ownership
The application source remains in ramideltoro/fantasy_football_edge. This monitoring change is deployed from local-server-observability by the infrastructure pipeline and does not modify the Fantasy application runtime.
expert:
## Health contract
SELECT 1 proves a limited database round trip. It does not validate schema migrations, data quality, import recency, connection-pool headroom or query performance under load. Treat the health measurement as a connectivity signal and keep those application-level concerns distinct.

## Independent frontend and backend checks
Separate targets make it possible to identify a reachable frontend with an unhealthy backend. The probe records TLS failure or missing HTTP response as unsuccessful, never as a healthy fallback. Timing ends at response headers and is not a browser rendering benchmark.

## Shared probe dependency
Monitoring runs on the local server. Internet or host failures can remove evidence for several sites simultaneously. Historical storage remains in Grafana Cloud, but an absent sample cannot establish that the Fantasy service itself is down. Consult last-check freshness and the local host dashboard.

## Further instrumentation
Importer age, request errors and process resource usage need dedicated application or host signals before they can be shown accurately. This view intentionally contains no fabricated values for those measurements.

title: Daily inspection and issue history
description: Coverage, issue lifecycle, bounded logs and encrypted history.
summary:
## What happens each day
GitHub Actions starts an inspection at 09:00 UTC. It checks available metrics, expected services and recurring error patterns, then publishes a report in the portal. GitHub may start scheduled work late; the report records the inspection window and delay. Owners can request another run after Google sign-in.

## What issue statuses mean
A first failure is New. A repeated failure is Ongoing. A completed check without that failure makes it Remediated. A returning failure is Reopened. When the source cannot be checked, the issue stays Unverified instead of being declared fixed.

## Read the coverage
Every report lists checked services, application relationships and missing instrumentation. A report with no findings is not proof of health if checks were incomplete. No email or messaging notifications are added.
technical:
## Scheduler and state
The infrastructure repository owns .github/workflows/inspect.yml. Runs share the host deployment concurrency group. The inspection cursor starts at the previous successful execution, capped at seven days; a cap creates incomplete coverage. State is atomically written to /var/lib/local-server-observability/state.json. Report summaries and issue transitions are retained indefinitely; detailed diagnostic evidence is pruned after 90 days.

## Deterministic checks
Resource checks use versioned thresholds: CPU and memory 90%, root filesystem 85%, public endpoint availability 99%, and TLS seven days. Local service health, restart counts and backup status use existing exporters. Explicit metric inspectionThreshold values apply to every host. Fallback limits require matching metric units and exact utilization, availability or certificate names: available-memory bytes and disk-throughput bytes per second are informational samples, not percentage violations. Genuine memory/disk utilization and Cloud alerts remain evaluated separately. Missing instrumentation remains an explicit incomplete check. Log inspection uses fixed selectors and a ten-query, 500-entry-per-query budget. Full forward pages defer all entries at their final timestamp and re-read that boundary, so tied logs cannot be lost or double-counted. A short final page proves exhaustion; a saturated single timestamp, exhausted budget, malformed response or failed query remains incomplete. A separate successful query must also prove fresh source activity. Evidence contains approved classifications and counts, never raw lines. Recurring-error thresholds and score weights are unchanged.

## AI and backups
After deterministic checks, an idle-only local Qwen request may summarize up to twelve finding groups. It runs once with a 60-second deadline, within the five-minute total allowance. Active inference connections, failure or invalid evidence references produce a template fallback. AI never changes lifecycle state. AES-256-GCM encrypted evidence backups are stored as 90-day Actions artifacts; encrypted summaries and transition histories are retained in the issue-history GitHub release. Each backup is decrypted and compared before upload.

## Verified backup restoration
The daily pipeline takes a consistent SQLite snapshot of owner Grafana, encrypts it separately, decrypts it in the runner and requires PRAGMA integrity_check to return ok. Both report bytes and database bytes must match their originals. Detailed evidence and owner database snapshots use 90-day encrypted artifacts. Indefinite summary archives live in a draft GitHub release so backup publication adds no release notifications. To recover, download the chosen Actions artifact using an authorized GitHub session, supply REPORT_BACKUP_KEY privately, and run services/workspace/backup.mjs decrypt input.enc output. Validate state JSON and SQLite integrity before replacing files. Stop only local-server-observability and observe-grafana-owner for replacement, preserve a rollback copy, restore ownership to observability, restart those two services and repeat the Qwen compatibility checks. Never replace the live SQLite database while Grafana is writing it.
expert:
## Remediation is a proof obligation
Absence of a failure is meaningful only if its relevant check completed. Inaccessible hosts, missing samples and truncated logs retain old issues as Unverified. Stable identity hashes the system, check and normalized failure signature, avoiding a new issue for every timestamp or repeated log entry. Lifecycle transitions are deterministic and never delegated to a model.

## Bounded evidence
Scanning arbitrary logs can expose credentials or amplify attacker-controlled instructions. The scanner executes only fixed metric and log queries, retains counts and approved classifications, and never executes log content. AI receives deterministic findings rather than raw logs. Suggested causes are hypotheses and must reference the supplied evidence IDs.

## Recovery limits
Encrypted backups protect stored history but still require the separately retained backup key. Detailed evidence expires; summaries remain. Offline or uninstrumented services cannot be made observable by a daily job alone, so coverage explicitly records those gaps. Scheduled execution can be delayed by GitHub, and a local-host outage prevents the local inspection process from running. Cloud remains an independent evidence source.

## Coverage verification
Initial deployment verified 60 Cloud dashboard definitions and six additional portal dashboards. The first inspection recorded 81 checks, including explicit gaps; later inspections also read every configured Cloud rule. Coverage counts are runtime evidence, not permanent constants. The original Raspberry Pi had no running application containers at discovery. Antenna Observatory and Skyglow were removed from the active fleet at the owner’s request on 2026-09-13. Historical reports remain intact. Mookie was retired from the fleet on September 20, 2026.

title: Edit and publish dashboards
description: Google owner access, synchronized originals and validated publishing.
summary:
## Make a copy
Sign in with Google and open owner Grafana. Synchronized originals are read-only. Use Save as to create an editable dashboard with a new identity. Your copies remain separate from the next Cloud synchronization.

## Publish a reviewed version
My dashboards includes Publish to Git. Enter the saved dashboard UID. The portal validates the panel types and approved queries, removes private metadata, and opens a pull request. Review and merge that pull request through the normal documentation and deployment pipeline.

## Keep private diagnostics private
Raw logs, traces and unrestricted queries stay in authenticated diagnostics. Publishing is limited to approved metric panels. A new query needs a reviewed registry change before it can appear publicly.
technical:
## Authentication and copies
The existing Google OAuth flow uses PKCE, nonce, browser-bound state and verified owner email claims. Only a verified session causes the proxy to set the trusted Grafana identity. User-supplied identity and authorization headers are discarded. Same-origin validation protects mutation requests. Grafana provisioning uses allowUiUpdates=false for source originals.

## Publish contract
POST /api/owner/publish requires an owner session and the production Origin. It reads the saved dashboard from owner Grafana, rejects provisioned originals, oversized content, unsupported panel types and unregistered queries, then creates a branch and PR in local-server-observability. Public output contains approved opaque query IDs and no private links or annotations.

## Synchronization boundary
Published dashboards have new published-prefixed identities. Scheduled Cloud synchronization writes only source originals and never saves back into editable workspace dashboards. GitHub remains the reviewed publishing path; public API routes cannot save, publish, change alerts or trigger an inspection.

## Provisioning identities
Owner datasource names are preserved by UID from the existing SQLite database. Deployment verifies both native Grafana health endpoints after synchronization.

Infrastructure-only deployments restart the portal to refresh its runtime configuration and coordinated release manifest, even when the portal Git revision is unchanged.
expert:
## Editing is not publishing
A saved owner dashboard can contain private operational context. The publishing action therefore constructs a new public representation rather than copying the database record directly. A query can be valid PromQL and still unsuitable for public use, so membership in the Git-managed registry is required.

## Preventing synchronization conflicts
Provisioning and interactive editing cannot safely share a mutable identity: the next file sync can overwrite UI changes. Distinct source, workspace and published identities make that ownership visible. A published PR does not mutate the owner copy, and a daily source update cannot replace its contents.

## Scope and limitations
Grafana Cloud plugins may not run in OSS; originals remain accessible through their Cloud links. Publishing supports reviewed native metric panels, not arbitrary plugins or dashboard scripts. The owner proxy grants an editor identity while Cloud datasource access remains read-only, preserving Cloud alert and notification ownership.

Grafana provisioning matches names while enforcing unique UIDs. Preserving saved names prevents a Cloud rename from being interpreted as a new datasource, and explicit health gates detect failures after systemd starts.

The inventory, operational system, native dashboard catalog and query registration no longer include Mookie. The deployment skips its former enrollment and telemetry verification. Ten explicitly owned Grafana alert rules are deleted with ownership checks and repeatable missing-rule handling. expert:
## Retirement

The owner confirmed removal from the fleet on September 20, 2026. Active inventory, operational checks, dashboard catalog, query registration and managed alerts were removed. Deployment no longer contacts this server. No server data, credentials or historical incident records were deleted. Raspberry monitoring retains its own metrics.

The Observe drill checks exact active system identities against the archived inventory and operational configuration, rather than a historical fixed fleet size. The old 29-system assertion failed after retirement; no passing restore credit is accepted until the corrected full drill succeeds.

title: Explainable system health
description: How percentages, coverage, deductions, and recovery are calculated.
summary:
## Read the score
Every server and application has a verified health percentage and a separate coverage percentage. Green is 95–100%, amber is 70–94%, and red is below 70%. Click any percentage to see what needs attention and how to improve it.

## Missing evidence matters
Missing checks earn no credit. A completely unobserved system says “0% verified · health unknown” in neutral styling. That does not mean the server is down. The fleet average counts each of the five servers and seven applications once. Critical problems stay highlighted above it.

## Recovery is specific
A working website cannot clear a failed backup. Daily findings remain deducted until the relevant completed inspection verifies recovery. Acknowledging an incident does not improve its score.
technical:
## Versioned scoring
The portal config/operations.json defines canonical checks, categories, severity, applicability, freshness, thresholds, dependencies, and improvement steps. Category weights are availability 35%, performance and freshness 20%, resources 20%, recovery 15%, and coverage 10%. Explicit inapplicability redistributes weight proportionally; missing instrumentation does not.

Critical, warning, and informational checks have weights 3, 2, and 1. Passing checks earn full credit, warning conditions half, and failed or unknown checks zero. Each detail includes the points lost, category contribution, evidence time, and coverage gap or collected evidence. The displayed score rounds down.

## Ceilings
An essential outage caps health at 25%; unresolved critical failure at 49%; warnings or incomplete required coverage at 94%. Canonical aliases deduplicate metric, alert, and daily evidence. The worst observation wins. Unverified failures keep their previous impact until a completed relevant check verifies recovery.

## Timing
A server-side collector runs every minute independently of page visits. Current health is labeled separately from historical charts. Coverage counts fresh, usable checks; score history includes indefinite daily summaries and 90 days of detailed samples.

Alloy binds loopback and uses CPUQuota=35%, MemoryMax=384M and a low scheduling priority. Enrollment does not alter receiver services or reboot the host.

## Worker dashboards
Eight per-stage dashboards expose scrape availability, readiness, expected production ownership, in-flight work, consumers and stage event rates using fixed job and service selectors. Missing readiness metrics remain unknown. Shadow ownership stays expected_active=0. Existing Cloudflare workers and production ingestion remain independent. RabbitMQ dashboards show ready and unacknowledged messages plus acknowledgement rate.

## Deployment
Update all three wiki modes and source-lock fingerprints before release. Merge documentation first, then infrastructure and portal changes; deploy the exact portal SHA through the serialized GitHub coordinator. Verify Cloud sample freshness, public health, dashboard datasource queries, five-host coverage, and Google protection for owner routes.

## Private investigation
New portal dashboards have native owner copies with the Cloud metrics datasource and host-scoped private logs where applicable. Raspberry and Mookie are accepted explicit scopes in the authenticated log API. Public queries remain registered and anonymous. HTTPS latency warns at 2 seconds and fails at the 8-second probe budget. Host checks and HTTP checks remain separate evidence.

## Production versus shadow evidence
Cloudflare production ingestion uses the backend-owned legacy-worker scheduled-run outcomes and success timestamps, scoped to job=nutsnews-backend-host and instance=backend.nutsnews.com. The similarly named nutsnews_worker_last_success_timestamp_seconds belongs to a shadow fetcher and must never be used as production success evidence. Scheduled-success age is displayed without an unverified cadence threshold. A regression test preserves this ownership separation.
