## Evidence and ownership
Discovery is observational. A repository name, historical Pages deployment or green CI run cannot establish current production ownership. Shadow worker health must remain visible without routing live ingestion to that worker. Production contract metrics and configuration take precedence over container naming. The two unhealthy shadow stages need a separate qualified release; simply restarting them would neither align their old images with source nor prove safe ownership.

## Migration boundary
Observe becomes the central presentation surface; Grafana Cloud remains the telemetry backend. Cloud originals and private diagnostics remain intact. Public dashboards use a fixed query registry and anonymous series labels. Only inventory metadata and approved numeric aggregates become public; logs, credentials, environment files and arbitrary query access stay behind owner authentication.

## Cardinality and load
Per-service systemd metrics use a fixed unit list. Application health is polled only on loopback with three-second deadlines; synthetic HTTPS checks have eight-second budgets. Eight worker stages are explicitly selected, with no feed URLs, article identifiers, user data or prompts used as new labels. Native dashboards fetch selected series on demand. Existing bounded public query concurrency remains in force.

## Recovery and verification limits
Pi enrollment preserves the OS, network settings and receiver processes. Previous Alloy configuration is backed up before replacement. Remove or disable only the new telemetry timer and Alloy service to reverse a first-time enrollment; never stop receiver services as a telemetry rollback. The local portal uses immutable releases and its existing activation rollback. Missing samples, old deployment snapshots, incomplete backup evidence and mobile runtime visibility remain explicit limitations. No synthetic test is a substitute for an isolated application restore test.

Live verification detected Alloy replacing the static journal job label with its component name. The inspection selector uses stable instance/project identity so collector upgrades do not silently lose log coverage. Owner dashboard links are verified native destinations, with log scope tied to the application host.

title: Actionable improvement checks
description: How Observe distinguishes verified problems from missing monitoring and incomplete history.
summary:
## Reading improvement statuses
Observe now connects available restart, backup, database, restore-drill and collector signals to health checks. Confirmed failures and warnings appear first. A missing database cloud snapshot is a real failure, not an unknown result.

## Evidence gaps
Setup required means that no scoped check has been registered. No data means a configured source has no fresh valid evidence. Collecting history means the 30-day availability window is incomplete. These states still reduce verified health and coverage; none means healthy. Expand a check for its specific next step.

## Safe operation
The repair changes monitoring queries and the portal. It does not activate shadow workers or restore application data. Application-specific recovery and performance requirements remain visible until evidence exists.
technical:
## Repaired sources
The PostgreSQL check uses pg_up scoped to the backend PostgreSQL exporter; the unexported postgresql@18-main systemd label previously made every dependent application unverified. Backend and VPS backup freshness use existing exporter contracts. PostgreSQL restore-drill and RabbitMQ recovery-stage gauges supply scoped recovery evidence. Backend, VPS and Mookie restart checks use hourly counter increases. Receiver coverage uses its collector timestamp.

## Probes and logs
A registered nutsnews-backend readiness probe now supplies response time and freshness. HTTPS probes use independent TLS connections so session reuse cannot drop certificate-expiry evidence. NutsNews Loki inspections select host rather than the absent instance label; Raspberry retains its project scope.

## Policies and presentation
Weekly local image backups warn after eight days and fail after nine. Daily local database cloud backups warn after 30 hours and fail after 48. Scheduled ingestion uses the existing 15-minute exporter contract, scoped to production backend ownership. Unknown remains the conservative machine status; evidenceState provides not-configured, no-data, collecting-history or policy-required presentation. Gaps earn zero health credit and no coverage. Probe-only coverage requires every registered probe and cannot override missing configured metrics.

## Evidence boundaries
A database restore-drill gauge proves only the named drill; it is not full-host recovery. RabbitMQ stage gauges report the existing recovery verification, without running a destructive drill. No source is synthesized for idle shadow-worker performance, unregistered application restore tests, or absent device backups. These requirements stay explicit and continue reducing health.

## Failure retention
Current critical failures and unresolved inspection findings remain authoritative. Missing samples never clear a previous failure. Deductions sort failures, then warnings, then evidence gaps by lost points. A stale collector overrides reason metadata to No data. Long-window availability stays Collecting history until the existing coverage requirement is met; missing minutes never become successes.

## Verification and rollback
Regression tests cover real probe registration, Loki label scopes, credential boundaries, source isolation and zero credit for missing evidence. Deployment uses the existing immutable release and rollback workflow. Verify public health, owner authentication boundaries, fresh samples and unchanged application process identities after activation. The API reason field is additive, preserving clients that interpret unknown conservatively.
